Question Choices: Select. A histogram has most data on the left and a long tail to the right. Identify the shape ~~Symmetrical | Left-tailed | Right-tailed | No-pattern~~
Hints: Follow the long tail, not the location of the peak.
Solution: A tail extending toward larger values on the right gives a right-tailed or right-skewed distribution.

Question Choices: Select. What does "symmetrical" mean? ~~One-side-is-longer | Both-sides-look-similar | Only-one-peak | Data-is-random~~
Hints: Follow the long tail, not the location of the peak.
Solution: A symmetric distribution has matching or approximately matching frequencies at equal distances on both sides of its center: the sides resemble mirror images.

Question Choices: What is an outlier? (A) Most common value   (B) A value far from others   (C) Middle value   (D) A group of values
Hints: Distinguish nearby groups, empty intervals, high-frequency areas, and isolated values.
Solution: An outlier is an observation unusually far from the rest of the distribution. Here a single isolated far-away value is the outlier, not the middle or most-common value.

Question Choices: What is a cluster? : (A) A single value   (B) A gap   (C) A group of data close together   (D) The largest value
Hints: Distinguish nearby groups, empty intervals, high-frequency areas, and isolated values.
Solution: C. A cluster is a group of observations close together on the value axis. It is neither a single isolated value nor an empty interval.
